programme.title: After Dark
programme.desc: After Dark was a British late night live discussion programme broadcast on Channel 4 television between 1987 and 1997, and on the BBC in 2003. Inspired by an Austrian programme called Club 2, Roly Keating of the BBC described it as "one of the great television talk formats of all time". In 2010 the television trade magazine Broadcast wrote "After Dark defined the first 10 years of Channel 4, just as Big Brother did for the second".

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Through the act of karanga, we traverse both the physical and spiritual realms, guided by ancestral voices that echo through time. This sacred practice is far more than a ritual—it is a powerful form of cultural expression that binds the living with those who have passed on. Within the context of Whiria te hono, a distinguished collective of kaikaranga from Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei, the spiritual and practical responsibilities of this tradition are deeply honoured and carefully upheld. These wāhine carry the weight of generations with each call, embodying the values, stories, and mana of their iwi. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Charlie Rahiri describes himself as a reluctant iwi leader. But he was destined by his kaumātua to lead his iwi, Ngati Ranginui. He’s a direct descendant of Iwi chief Paraone Koikoi who surrendered his guns and pouches to the colonial office in 1864, only to be back in his kainga in Taumata three years later fighting for his land by pulling up survey pegs. We look at the changing role of a Māori Leader in Modern society through the eyes of Charlie Rahiri. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: From haka to anthem—Te Arawa shares the stories behind powerful songs that preserve our past and move hearts worldwide. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: The life and practice of Kumeroa Gregory, a skilled rongoā and weaving practitioner. Raised in Te Urewera under the guidance of her kuia and koroua, Ruakenana, Kumeroa’s journey took a significant turn in 1970 when she moved north. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: we cross the waters of Tauranga Moana to the island of Matakana. There, we meet the people of Oruarahi Marae and explore the rich histories of the land and their ancestor, Te Rangihouhiri. We journey back to a time when Oruarahi was thriving, tracing how the marae fell into disrepair, and hear the powerful story of its awakening and restoration — and what it took to bring the marae back to life. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Long dormant, the ancient wisdom of our female deities is a crucial blueprint for modern life. Tinamaree Kaipara-Winitana and Hana Tapiata show how to reclaim their knowledge and live by their light once more. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: We step back to honour the history of the coronation, recognising how each iwi and hapū has a unique role in shaping the beauty and strength of the Koroneihana. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Māori entrepreneurs Piripi Winiata, Te Uranga Lee-Belk and Peter Lucas explain why it’s important for future generations to understand history behind the Māori economy and investment, in order to build sustainable wealth as part of a wider self-autonomy (mana motuhake) movement. (R)

programme.title: Masterstroke
programme.desc: Wall Street bankers voted themselves $28 billion in bonuses, while 2.8 billion people struggled on less than $2 per day. What can the history of art teach us about the rights and wrongs of money?

programme.title: Live at Psalter Studio
programme.desc: From banging on kitchen pots to playing the keyboard, music has always been something that Jayneen has loved doing, believing our ability to create music is a reflection of being made in His image.

programme.title: Cliff!
programme.desc: Maybe you remember Paul the Octopus and his predictions during the world cup? Well there is an interesting thing we can learn about Paul and predictions.

programme.title: Line Upon Line
programme.desc: "Is it a sin to dream about sinning?" Pastors John and Wes offer Bible answers to this question and more in episode 7 of season 4.

programme.title: Amazing Discoveries
programme.desc: Mark Finley looks at the fatal attraction of cults, and who we are really worshipping if it is not the God of heaven

programme.title: Classical Destinations
programme.desc: Explore a rich cultural journey with the heritage of classical music in Great Britain - its influence, composers, and iconic venues.

programme.title: Revolutionary
programme.desc: Sergio Gonzalez and Oleg Kostyuk delve deep into the character of Jesus Christ and uncover his revolutionary actions that led to the disruption of the political world in the 1st century AD.

programme.title: The Incredible Journey
programme.desc: Amazing Grace, sung over 10 million times each year, was written by a notorious blasphemer, rebellious shipman and slave trader, who became a church minister and an abolitionist

programme.title: Take Time To Dance
programme.desc: A drama about a Christian family law attorney and ballroom dancer who investigates a mysterious divorce case involving a couple who appeared to have a happy marriage

programme.title: Authentic
programme.desc: War zones like Ukraine, dreadful pandemics like COVID-19, senseless violence and death. Does God care? Shawn Boonstra looks for answers in part 2 of our series on the problem of evil.

programme.title: Digging Deeper
programme.desc: Is the Mark of the Beast a chip, a card or something much more sinister? People from diverse faith backgrounds meet with evangelist Mark Finley to discuss the Mark of the Beast.

programme.title: Wild Britain
programme.desc: In this series, Ray Mears explores some of Britain's most beautiful areas of natural beauty, to uncover the fascinating wild life that lives there. This week he explores the Yorkshire Dales.

programme.title: Life Changer
programme.desc: Dr Ross Grant examines some of the latest research into depression, and looks for ways we can make adolescents resistant to depression.

programme.title: Answers In Genesis
programme.desc: Ken Ham explores the impact of Darwin's theory of evolution on society.

programme.title: Hope At Night
programme.desc: What does the fossil record reveal about Earth's past? Explore fossils, geology and genetics as scientists examine competing explanations for the history of life and our world.

programme.title: Stupid Money
programme.desc: Daniel Reed of Nova Home Works built his business the hard way, by going into debt. When he realized that was not the best way to operate, things began to change.

programme.title: Tracing the Footsteps of Jesus
programme.desc: Take a fascinating and insightful journey with presenter Tony Moore as he retraces the footsteps of Jesus through the ancient Bible lands
